style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The song of the city -- Zion seen from inside her walls after a siege that broke before it began. The LORD is great and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, on His holy mountain: beautiful in its height, the joy of the whole earth, the city of the great King. The kings assembled, crossed over together, saw -- and were stunned, panicked, and fled, seized by trembling like a woman in labor, shattered like Tarshish ships in an east wind. Whether the occasion was Sennacherib's army melting away in 701 or another deliverance, the congregation draws the lesson on the spot: as we had heard, so now we have seen; God will establish this city forever. Then they do what pilgrims do: think about His covenant love inside the temple, and walk the walls -- count the towers, mark the ramparts, go through the citadels -- so that they can describe it to the next generation. And the last line turns the architecture into a confession: this God is our God forever and ever; He Himself will guide us even to death. Hebrews 12:22 gives the city its final address: the heavenly Jerusalem.

1.text: A song, a psalm of the sons of Korah. The LORD is great and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, on the mountain of His holiness.
1.amp: A Song [shir] and Psalm [mizmor] for ['of', the KJV margin] the sons [ben] of Korah [Qorach]. Great [gadol] is the LORD [YHWH], and greatly [meod] to be praised [halal] in the city [ir] of our God [Elohim], in the mountain [har] of His holiness [qodesh].
1.notes: gadol YHWH u-mehullal meod (H1419, H3068, H1984, H3966): great is the LORD and greatly to be praised -- Psalm 145:3's opening line, now given an address -- be-ir Elohenu har-qodsho (H5892, H430, H2022, H6944): in the city of our God, His holy mountain. The greatness is universal; the praise has a street.

2.text: Beautiful in its height, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north -- the city of the great King.
2.amp: Beautiful [yapheh] for situation [noph -- elevation], the joy [masos] of the whole earth [eretz], is mount [har] Zion [Tsiyyon], on the sides [yerekah] of the north [tsaphon], the city [qiryah] of the great [rav] King [melek].
2.notes: yepheh noph mesos kol-ha-aretz (H3303, H5131, H4885, H776): beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth -- har-Tsiyyon yarkete tsaphon (H2022, H6726, H3411, H6828): Zion 'on the sides of the north', Zaphon was the sacred mountain of Baal in Canaanite poetry (cf. Isaiah 14:13), and many hear the psalm claiming that title for Jerusalem. qiryat melek rav (H7151, H4428, H7227): city of the great King -- the words Jesus quotes in Matthew 5:35.

3.text: God, in her citadels, has made Himself known as a high stronghold.
3.amp: God [Elohim] is known [yada] in her palaces [armon -- citadels] for a refuge [misgab -- high stronghold].
3.notes: Elohim be-armenoteha noda le-misgab (H430, H759, H3045, H4869): God has made Himself KNOWN in the citadels as a misgab, the unscalable height of Psalms 46 and 62. The walls are not the defense; the God in the walls is.

4.text: For look: the kings met by appointment; together they crossed over toward her.
4.amp: For, lo, the kings [melek] were assembled [yaad -- met by appointment], they passed by [abar] together [yachad].
4.notes: ki-hinneh ha-melakhim noadu (H4428, H3259): the kings MET -- yaad is to convene by appointment, a coalition -- aberu yachdav (H5674, H3162): they advanced together. Sennacherib's host, whose 'princes are altogether kings' (Isaiah 10:8), or the Moab-Ammon-Edom alliance that marched on Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20); the psalm does not name them.

5.text: They saw it -- and so they were stunned; they were thrown into panic; they fled in haste.
5.amp: They saw [raah] it, and so they marvelled [tamah -- were astonished]; they were troubled [bahal -- thrown into panic], and hasted away [chaphaz -- fled in alarm].
5.notes: hemmah rau ken tamahu (H7200, H8539): they saw, and so they were stunned -- nibhalu nechpazu (H926, H2648): panicked, fled in haste -- one verb of sight and three verbs of collapse in a single verse, Psalm 6's bahal and Psalm 116's chaphaz. What they saw is not said; the city was enough.

6.text: Trembling seized them there -- pain, like a woman in labor.
6.amp: Fear [raadah -- trembling] took hold [achaz] upon them there, and pain [chil -- writhing], as of a woman in travail [yalad -- giving birth].
6.notes: raadah achazatam sham (H7461, H270): trembling GRIPPED them there -- chil ka-yoledah (H2427, H3205): the writhing of a woman giving birth, the Old Testament's standard image for sudden, inescapable anguish (cf. Isaiah 13:8). The besiegers in labor; the city at peace.

7.text: With an east wind You shatter the ships of Tarshish.
7.amp: You break [shabar -- shatter] the ships [oniyyah] of Tarshish [Tarshish] with an east [qadim] wind [ruach].
7.notes: be-ruach qadim teshabber oniyyot Tarshish (H7307, H6921, H7665, H591, H8659): the east wind -- the sirocco off the desert -- shattering the Tarshish ships, the big ocean-going merchantmen of the age (cf. 1 Kings 22:48). The image shifts from land to sea: the coalition broken like a fleet in a gale.

8.text: What we had heard, we have now seen with our own eyes, in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God: God makes her stand firm forever. Selah.
8.amp: As we have heard [shama], so have we seen [raah] in the city [ir] of the LORD [YHWH] of hosts [tsaba], in the city of our God [Elohim]: God will establish [kun] it for [ad] ever [olam]. Selah [selah].
8.notes: ka-asher shamanu ken rainu (H8085, H7200): the hinge of the psalm -- what the fathers told us, we have now watched happen -- be-ir YHWH tsebaot (H5892, H3068, H6635), the city of the LORD of armies, be-ir Elohenu (H430), in the city of our God; Elohim yekhoneneha ad-olam (H430, H3559, H5704, H5769): God will keep it standing forever. Tradition became eyewitness.

9.text: We have pondered Your covenant love, O God, in the midst of Your temple.
9.amp: We have thought [damah -- pondered, compared] of Your lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love], O God [Elohim], in the midst [qereb] of Your temple [hekal].
9.notes: dimminu Elohim chasdekha (H1819, H430, H2617): damah is 'to liken, to weigh in the mind' -- the congregation turning covenant love over in thought -- be-qereb hekhalekha (H7130, H1964): inside the temple, after the siege lifted. Worship as reflection on what just happened.

10.text: As Your name is, O God, so is Your praise, to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is filled with righteousness.
10.amp: According to Your name [shem], O God [Elohim], so is Your praise [tehillah] unto the ends [qatseh] of the earth [eretz]: Your right hand [yamin] is full [male] of righteousness [tsedek].
10.notes: ke-shimkha Elohim ken tehillatekha (H8034, H430, H8416): praise sized to the Name -- al-qatsve-eretz (H7099, H776): to the earth's ends; tsedeq maleah yeminekha (H6664, H4390, H3225): Your right hand full of righteousness -- the hand that broke the coalition was doing justice, not merely winning.

11.text: Let Mount Zion rejoice, let Judah's daughters be glad, on account of Your judgments.
11.amp: Let mount [har] Zion [Tsiyyon] rejoice [samach], let the daughters [bath] of Judah [Yehudah] be glad [gil -- exult], because of Your judgments [mishpat].
11.notes: yismach har-Tsiyyon (H8055, H2022, H6726), tagelnah benot Yehudah (H1523, H1323, H3063): the mountain and the towns around it -- the 'daughters' of a city are its villages -- or, as some take it, the women of Judah who led the victory songs (cf. 1 Samuel 18:6) -- le-maan mishpatekha (H4941): because of Your judgments. Psalm 97:8's line: judgment as the faithful's good news.

12.text: Walk around Zion; go all the way round her; count her towers.
12.amp: Walk about [savav] Zion [Tsiyyon], and go round about [naqaph -- encircle] her: tell [saphar -- count] the towers [migdal] thereof.
12.notes: sobbu Tsiyyon ve-haqqiphuha (H5437, H6726, H5362): the pilgrims sent on a circuit of the walls -- siphru migdaleha (H5608, H4026): COUNT her towers. Nehemiah 12:31-39 records a procession along that very wall; the point of the count is the next verse.

13.text: Set your heart on her ramparts; pass through and consider her citadels -- so that you may tell it to the generation to come.
13.amp: Mark ye well ['Set your heart to', shith leb, the KJV margin] her bulwarks [chel -- ramparts], consider ['raise up', pasag -- go through, examine, the KJV margin] her palaces [armon -- citadels]; that ye may tell [saphar] it to the generation [dor] following [acharon -- the one after].
13.notes: shitu libbekhem le-chelah (H7896, H3820, H2430): the margin's literal -- SET YOUR HEART on her rampart -- passegu armenoteha (H6448, H759): examine the citadels -- le-maan tesapperu le-dor acharon (H5608, H1755, H314): so you can recount it to the generation after. The inspection is for the children; every tower counted is a testimony stored.

14.text: For this God is our God forever and ever; He Himself will guide us even to death.
14.amp: For this God [Elohim] is our God for ever [olam] and ever [ad]: He will be our guide [nahag -- lead, drive] even unto death [muth].
14.notes: ki zeh Elohim Elohenu olam va-ed (H430, H5769, H5703): THIS God -- the one who did this, here -- is our God forever; hu yenahagenu al-mut (H5090, H4192): He will drive us on, shepherd us, to death -- or, as some read the Hebrew, 'beyond death'; the ancient Greek reads 'forever' (olamot). The walk around the walls ends at the grave's edge with a Guide still ahead.
